title_ar: الضوابط الشرعية لفهم الكتاب والسنة -الجزء الثاني
title_en: The Legal Controls for Understanding the Book and the Sunnah — Part Two
body_ar: ومستويات الناس في هذا متباينة متمايزة يمكن أن نفصلها بالأرقام ليكون ذلك أدعى للانتباه، فالرقم الأول في الناس في فهم كتاب الله وسنة رسوله (ص) من لا يفهم العربية أصلا، المطبق الذي لا يفهم العربية، فهذا حظه من دلالة النصوص التقليد في دلالتها كما يقلد في نقلها، لأننا ذكرنا أن الكتاب والسنة يبحث فيهما من جهتين، جهة الورود وجهة الدلالة، جهة الورود معناه الثبوت، ونحن في القرآن حصل لدينا العلم الجازم بالتواتر به وهو معصوم محفوظ فلا يحتاج اليوم إلى التفصيل في الأسانيد والتدقيق في تراجم الرجال لكن الإسناد مطلوب على كل حال وهو من خصائص هذه الأمة وقد شرف الله به هذه الأمة من بين الأمم ولذلك يقول أهل الحديث: كفى بالرجل شرفا أن يكون اسمه أدنى سلسلة أسماها اسم رسول الله (ص)..
body_en: And people's levels in this are various and distinct from one another. We can set them out by numbers, so that this may better hold the attention. The first rank among people in understanding the Book of God and the sunnah of His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, is the one who does not understand Arabic at all — the one entirely without Arabic. This person's share of the signification of the texts is to follow a qualified scholar (taqlīd) in what they signify, just as he follows one in their transmission. For we have said that the Book and the sunnah are examined from two sides: the side of their coming down to us, and the side of their signification. The side of their coming down to us means their establishment. In the case of the Qur'an, we have attained certain knowledge of it by mass transmission (tawātur), and it is preserved and protected, so there is no need today for detailed work on the chains of transmission or close scrutiny of the biographies of the transmitters. But the chain of transmission (isnād) is called for in any case, and it is one of the distinguishing features of this community, by which God has honoured this community from among the communities. That is why the people of hadith say: it is honour enough for a man that his name should be the lowest link in a chain whose highest is the name of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him..

flags.note: al-muṭbiq is doing intensifying work here — 'complete, total' — but the construction is unusual and the source is unvowelled, so the reading is not certain. It might also be a transcription slip. The English takes the intensifying reading, which fits the context of a graded scale, and the reading is flagged rather than assumed.

flags.arabic: كفى بالرجل شرفا أن يكون اسمه أدنى سلسلة أسماها اسم رسول الله
flags.context: the saying attributed to the people of hadith
options: render with 'lowest' and 'highest' as the Arabic's adnā/asmā have it
render as 'at the bottom of a chain whose summit is the Prophet'
flags.note: The Arabic plays on adnā (lowest/nearest) against asmā (highest/most exalted), and the spatial figure of the chain is the point. The Sheikh attributes the saying to 'the people of hadith' collectively and names no one; nothing has been supplied.

translator_notes: The date carried here is the CMS record date. Across this whole slice the site serves a bulk-upload timestamp of 19-21 December 2010, which is when the written archive was loaded into the site, not when the Sheikh gave the answer or delivered the lecture. date_is_cms_upload is set true. The real date of composition is not recoverable from the page and has not been guessed.

The source writes the eulogy after the Prophet's name sometimes in full (صلى الله عليه وسلم) and sometimes as the abbreviation (ص). Both are rendered in English as 'peace and blessings be upon him'; the source form is preserved in body_ar.

This record is Part Two of a two-part lecture; Part One is record 579. Both are excerpts and both carry the same CMS timestamp of 21 December 2010 13:29.
'The side of their coming down to us' renders jihat al-wurūd, which the Sheikh immediately glosses himself as al-thubūt, establishment. Both have been kept because his gloss is part of the text.
'Mass transmission' for tawātur and 'chain of transmission' for isnād follow the glossary entries for mutawātir and sanad.
Unlike record 579 this part carries no khuṭbat al-ḥājah, because the page begins in the middle of the lecture.
